translations.translatedText: # Wednesday 1.7.2020 (radio)
The storm caused damage in Eastern Finland. Restrictions on public events are easing. A record number of children have been placed outside their homes. There were many hot days in June.
The TV Clear News has a summer break and will continue on 17.8.
The radio Clear News is made every day, including in summer.
## Summer storm knocked down trees
![A tree fallen onto a house in the storm.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-11427155)
Open image viewer
The storm dropped a large branch onto a house in Nilsiä. Photo: Lasse Kurronen
The summer storm has been battering Eastern Finland.
The summer storm Päivö brought heavy rain and strong wind to the whole country yesterday. The storm hit Eastern Finland hardest during the night.

The Energy Industry says that perhaps as many as 100,000 households were left without electricity when the storm knocked trees onto power lines. Electricity companies say it may take many days before all the faults are repaired.

The storm also knocked trees onto roads, houses and cars. In addition, the strong wind tore off, for example, metal roofs and boats. Rescue services had about 1,000 call-outs in total because of the storm.
The storm also caused faults in the mobile phone network and disrupted train traffic.

The Finnish Meteorological Institute says that the strongest wind gusts and the largest amounts of rain were measured in North Savo. The strongest wind gusts, over 27 metres per second, were measured in Kuopio. The most rain fell in Pielavesi, where over 90 millimetres fell in 24 hours.
## Easing for public events
![Audience following at a safe distance the athletics invitational competition "Uusi Alku" on 7 June 2020 in Lahti.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-11393519)
Open image viewer
Audience at the athletics invitational competition in Lahti in early June. Photo: Roni Rekomaa / Lehtikuva
Corona restrictions on public events are easing a little.
From today, events with more than 500 people may be held outdoors.
Safety at events must still be ensured, however. Safe distances and good hygiene must still be kept, for example.
In Finland, 22 new corona infections have been found in the past day. No new corona deaths have been reported for 2 days.
## June was warmer
![Children playing in water on a beach.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_extract,w_6000,h_3375,x_0,y_497/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,ar_16:9,dpr_1/f_auto/39-6930765ef46f2f80ceb/1593105259)
Open image viewer
Children play on the beach. Photo: Petteri Bülow / Yle
June was record warm this year, says the Finnish Meteorological Institute.
There were the most hot days in over 60 years. Hot temperatures were measured somewhere in Finland on a total of 21 days. Heat means a temperature of over 25 degrees.
The highest temperature of the month was 33.5 degrees. It was measured in Kankaanpää on 25 June, that is, last Thursday.
